title: Pure Alacrity production file
description: What Pure Alacrity's production reader accepts: AH.V1.importBlob (every production file goes through it: Productions → Load, Transfer Bay, Use with ChatGPT), the AH.Hydrate.fromBlob chain that fills each store, and the AH.AiKit normaliser in front of it. Derived from that code and measured at runtime by importing a file with a unique token in every field and reading which store and which screen shows it. 'x-store' is the per-production storage key (suffixed with the production id); 'x-screen' is where a person sees it. Unknown fields are allowed: they are kept in the production record, and the Use with ChatGPT check names each one. Joins are by scene NUMBER (scenes[].n), never by heading.

_alacrityProduction.description: Marks a production file. With it, every loader creates a NEW production. The Use with ChatGPT panel also accepts a file without it that has a production and scenes, and says so.

_exportedBy.description: Written by Use with ChatGPT → Send to ChatGPT: "Pure Alacrity · Use with ChatGPT". Keep it when you return an edited export.

_sourceProductionId.description: The production the export came from. Informational: the import always makes a new production.

production.description: Merged into the file by AH.V1.importBlob. name, type, status, client, director, logline (or synopsis / description) and budget reach the production card; the rest is kept in the production record (dc_alacrity_prod_<id>).

name.description: The production's title. Falls back to title, then to the file name.

title.description: Used as the name when name is missing.

status.description: Upper-cased. The card colours BID, R&D, PRE-PROD, IN PROD, POST, WRAP, SHELVED.

logline.description: Shown on the card as the description.

budget.description: Text with the currency sign, e.g. "$25,000" or "$1.5M". A bare number is rewritten as money by the normaliser (it used to show $0 on the card).

script.description: The screenplay. Give `fountain` (the whole script as Fountain text) and the normaliser reads it with the app's own parser into `lines`; or give `lines` in the app's line model. A plain string is read as Fountain. x-store ah_script_; x-screen Script Studio.

fountain.description: Fountain text. [[ ]] before the first heading becomes the manual (front matter); [[ ]] after a heading becomes that scene's director's note; # pathway and * choice lines make it a branching (Interactive) script.

titlePage.description: Wins over the Fountain title page.

format.description: Set to "interactive" automatically when the Fountain has branching markers; otherwise "screenplay".

dirNotes.description: Director's notes keyed by the index of the scene-heading line. Prefer [[ ]] under the heading in the Fountain, which survives edits.

lines.description: The app's line model. Types: scene action char dial paren trans centered pathway choice.

scenes.description: One row per scene heading, in script order. x-store ah_scenes_; x-screen Stripboard, Schedule, Call sheet, Shooting schedule. The reader folds number/scene → n, heading/slug → title, location → loc, intExt → int.

n.description: Scene number: "1", "2", "3A". Unique. Shots, breakdown rows and risks join on it.

heading.description: The heading exactly as in the script, node tag included, e.g. "EXT. LEVEL CROSSING - NIGHT [N00]".

loc.description: The set, without INT./EXT. and without the time of day.

pages.description: Eighths as text: "1 2/8", "3/8". An estimate; the app re-measures from the script.

day.description: Shoot day the scene is scheduled on: "D01", "D02".

cast.description: Performers. Stored with crew in ah_cast_ (dept defaults to CAST). x-screen Cast & Crew, Contacts, Call sheet (rows without a name are left off the call sheet).

name.description: The performer. "" when nobody is cast.

scriptChar.description: The character exactly as the cue spells it ("MAYA"). This is the link to the script.

crew.description: Crew. Stored with cast in ah_cast_ (dept defaults to CREW).

locations.description: x-store ah_loc_; x-screen Locations. name ⇄ n, status ⇄ st, notes ⇄ note are both written.

breakdown.description: One row per scene. x-store ah_bdown_; x-screen Breakdown (and Shopping reads the props). `breakdownRows` and `breakdowns` are accepted as the same thing.

shotlist.description: x-store ah_shots_ (normalised by the shot reader); x-screen Shot List, Shooting Schedule. `shots` is accepted as the same thing.

prepMin.description: Minutes to set up; drives the time-linked Shooting Schedule.

budgetLines.description: x-store ah_budget_lines_; x-screen Budget, which reads cat / name / est / act. category → cat, line / item / description → name, amount / estimate / cost → est are mapped by the normaliser (they used to show nothing).

risks.description: x-store ah_risk_; x-screen Risk, which reads t / s / lvl / mit. title / risk → t, scene → s, severity / level / impact → lvl, mitigation → mit are mapped by the normaliser (they used to show an empty table).

milestones.description: x-store ah_ms_; x-screen Milestones, Timeline. name / n / title, date / d / dueDate / due and status / st are all written.

devNotes.description: x-store ah_devnotes_; x-screen Dev Notes, which reads title / body (note → body is mapped).

tech.description: x-store ah_tech_; read by Equipment only while the production has no equipment list of its own.

coverage.description: Script coverage. x-store ah_coverage_. Fields: title writer form genre pages logline synopsis strengths concerns suggestions characterNotes marketability comps comments rec reader date scores.

documents.description: x-store ah_library_; x-screen Library. `library` is accepted as the same thing.

ipBible.description: x-store ah_ipbible_; x-screen IP & World Bible. title premise themes world characters.

post.description: x-store ah_post_; x-screen Post & Delivery. pipeline[] deliverables[] clearances[].

scripts.description: Several drafts; the one with active:true becomes the script. x-store ah_scripts_.

scheduleStrips.description: Stored exactly as given in ah_scenes_ (no normalising). Prefer scenes.

schedule.description: Older strip format: { strips: [ {type:'daybreak'|'banner'|'scene', scene, description, location, intExt, pages} ] }. Prefer scenes.

storymap.description: Not reliable in a production file: the app builds the story map from the script, and once it has, this section is dropped (measured). Use # pathways and * choices in the script, or a .pure map.

songsync.description: x-store ah_songsync_. songTitle artist durationSec sections[].

stills.description: x-store ah_stills_. Images as data URIs; never ask ChatGPT for these.
